# Superpowers

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## Table of Contents

- [How it works](#how-it-works)
- [Commercial Services](#commercial-services)
- [Getting Started](#installation)
  - [Claude Code](#claude-code)
  - [Antigravity](#antigravity)

  - [Cursor](#cursor)
  - [Devin CLI](#devin-cli)
  - [Factory Droid](#factory-droid)
  - [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli)
  - [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli)
  - [Grok Build CLI](#grok-build-cli)
  - [Kimi Code](#kimi-code)
  - [OpenCode](#opencode)
  - [Pi](#pi)

- [Community](#community)

- [Philosophy](#philosophy)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [Updating](#updating)
- [License](#license)
- [Visual companion telemetry](#visual-companion-telemetry)

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

## Commercial Services

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

## Installation

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

### Claude Code

Superpowers is available via the [official Claude plugin marketplace](https://claude.com/plugins/superpowers)

#### Official Marketplace

- Install the plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official
  ```

#### Superpowers Marketplace

The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin from this marketplace:

  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Antigravity

Install Superpowers as a plugin from this repository:

```bash
agy plugin install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
```

Antigravity lists each installed skill's description, and the description of
the `using-superpowers` skill prompts the model to load that skill at the start
of a conversation. Reinstall with the same command to update.

### Codex App

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- In the Codex app, click on Plugins in the sidebar.
- You should see `Superpowers` in the Coding section.
- Click the `+` next to Superpowers and follow the prompts.

### Codex CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Codex plugin marketplace](https://github.com/openai/plugins).

- Open the plugin search interface:

  ```bash
  /plugins
  ```

- Search for Superpowers:

  ```bash
  superpowers
  ```

- Select `Install Plugin`.

### Cursor

- In Cursor Agent chat, install from marketplace:

  ```text
  /add-plugin superpowers
  ```

- Or search for "superpowers" in the plugin marketplace.

### Devin CLI

- Install the plugin from this repository:

  ```bash
  devin plugins install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update to the latest version with:

  ```bash
  devin plugins update superpowers
  ```

### Factory Droid

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  droid plugin install superpowers@superpowers
  ```

### Gemini CLI

- Install the extension:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  gemini extensions update superpowers
  ```

### GitHub Copilot CLI

- Register the marketplace:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace
  ```

- Install the plugin:

  ```bash
  copilot plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

### Grok Build CLI

Superpowers is available via the [official Grok plugin marketplace](https://github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace).

- Install the plugin from xAI's official marketplace:

  ```bash
  grok plugin install superpowers@xai-official --trust
  ```

- Or open the marketplace in the TUI, search for Superpowers, and install it:

  ```text
  /marketplace
  ```

### Kimi Code

Superpowers is available in Kimi Code's plugin marketplace.

- Open Kimi Code's plugin manager:

  ```text
  /plugins
  ```

- Go to `Marketplace` > `Superpowers` and install it.

- Or install directly from this repository:

  ```text
  /plugins install https://github.com/obra/superpowers
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.kimi.md](docs/README.kimi.md)

### OpenCode

OpenCode uses its own plugin install; install Superpowers separately even if you
already use it in another harness.

- Tell OpenCode:

  ```
  Fetch and follow instructions from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/obra/superpowers/refs/heads/main/.opencode/INSTALL.md
  ```

- Detailed docs: [docs/README.opencode.md](docs/README.opencode.md)

### Pi

Install Superpowers as a Pi package from this repository:

```bash
pi install git:github.com/obra/superpowers
```

For local development, run Pi with this checkout loaded as a temporary package:

```bash
pi -e /path/to/superpowers
```

The Pi package loads the Superpowers skills and a small extension that injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and again after compaction. Pi has native skills, so no compatibility `Skill` tool is required. Subagent and task-list tools remain optional Pi companion packages.

### Qwen Code

Qwen Code installs plugins from Claude Code marketplaces directly.

- Install the plugin from this repository, and pick `superpowers` when prompted:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions install obra/superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  qwen extensions update superpowers
  ```

### Hermes Agent

Install Superpowers as a Hermes plugin from this repository:

```bash
hermes plugins install obra/superpowers --enable
```

Restart any active Hermes sessions after installing. Note: Hermes has no
post-compaction hook, so a very long session that compacts over its first
turn loses the bootstrap — start a fresh session if skills stop triggering.

### Muse

Superpowers is available as a native Muse plugin — same repo, same skills, all harnesses. The `using-superpowers` bootstrap is injected via the native `SessionStart` hook alongside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Pi, and the rest — no per-session opt-in.

- Install from a local checkout:

  ```bash
  muse plugins install ./
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

  Or clone and install:

  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git
  muse plugins install ./superpowers
  muse plugins approve superpowers
  ```

- Update later:

  ```bash
  muse plugins update superpowers
  ```

Restart any active Muse sessions after installing so the `SessionStart` hook takes effect — skills are active immediately, hooks require approval on first install. To verify, start a fresh session and send `Let's make a react todo list` — a working install auto-triggers `brainstorming` before any code is written. Version is tracked in `.version-bump.json` so `scripts/bump-version.sh` keeps it in sync.

## The Basic Workflow

1. **brainstorming** - Activates before building anything. Draws out what you actually want, and why, through questions that get you describing it, then plays its understanding back for correction. Small changes get agreed in chat; projects get a written design document a builder could plan from.

2. **using-git-worktrees** - Activates after design approval. Creates isolated workspace on new branch, runs project setup, verifies clean test baseline.

3. **writing-plans** - Activates with approved design. Breaks work into bite-sized tasks (2-5 minutes each). Every task has exact file paths, complete code, verification steps.

4. **subagent-driven-development** or **executing-plans** - Activates with plan. Either dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough), or implements every task inline in the current session with one fresh review of the whole branch at the end (cheapest).

5. **test-driven-development** - Activates during implementation. Enforces RED-GREEN-REFACTOR: write failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit. Deletes code written before tests.

6. **requesting-code-review** - Activates between tasks. Reviews against plan, reports issues by severity. Critical issues block progress.

7. **finishing-a-development-branch** - Activates when tasks complete. Verifies tests, presents options (merge/PR/keep/discard), cleans up worktree.

**The agent checks for relevant skills before any task.** Mandatory workflows, not suggestions.

## When Something Goes Wrong

Sometimes a session misbehaves: a skill fires when it shouldn't, stays silent when it should, or the agent ignores its plan, repeats work, or burns more tokens than you'd expect. Ask your coding agent to "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in this session" and it will invoke the **diagnosing-superpowers** skill. To examine an earlier session, name it: "figure out what went wrong with superpowers in session `<id>`".

The skill reads the session transcript, reports what happened with line-level evidence, and, if you want, packages a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

## Community

Superpowers is built by [Jesse Vincent](https://blog.fsck.com) and the rest of the folks at [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com).

- **Discord**: [Join us](https://discord.gg/35wsABTejz) for community support, questions, and sharing what you're building with Superpowers
- **Issues**: https://github.com/obra/superpowers/issues
- **Release announcements**: [Sign up](https://primeradiant.com/superpowers/) to get notified about new versions

## What's Inside

### Skills Library

**Testing**
- **test-driven-development** - RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle (includes testing anti-patterns reference)

**Debugging**
- **systematic-debugging** - 4-phase root cause process (includes root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting techniques)
- **verification-before-completion** - Ensure it's actually fixed
- **diagnosing-superpowers** - Work out what went wrong in a session, with evidence; export a scrubbed bundle or file an issue

**Collaboration** 
- **brainstorming** - Drawing out intent before building
- **writing-plans** - Detailed implementation plans
- **executing-plans** - Inline plan execution: one context, one final review
- **dispatching-parallel-agents** - Concurrent subagent workflows
- **requesting-code-review** - Pre-review ch

# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Fifty themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## Themes
Dusk
Closewise, bank reconciliation		 Cobalt
Relay, a webhook API		 Studio
Field Office, an identity studio		 Atelier
Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier		 Ribbon
Lull, a sleep sounds app
Furrow
Fieldbook, farm records		 Dose
Tandem, a family medication app		 Refract
Bellwater Lido, an outdoor pool		 Vantage
Swath, construction site scans		 Hedgerow
Five Mile Gin, a distillery
Ten of the fifty. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in [`references/themes/`](skills/hallmark/references/themes/) with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com). ## Custom Say **custom** and Hallmark drops the themes: no plan, no components, no palette recipe, only the floor, the gates and a short direction in [`direction.md`](skills/hallmark/references/direction.md) to find one idea that only this client has and let it run the page. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Redesign Hallmark never starts on a design that already exists unless you name it: ``` /hallmark redesign ./src/app /hallmark audit ./index.html ``` A full redesign keeps the content and the wiring and changes the system and the layout; say *keep the layout* for a restyle or *polish* for only the tells. `sloplint --before` records every link, field, handler and heading first, `sloplint --kept` fails the redesign if one went missing, and the handoff is a side-by-side before and after. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*. ## Inspired by [Impeccable](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable) · [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/frontend-design) · [Open Design](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design) · [Kami](https://github.com/tw93/kami) · [taste-skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill) · [huashu-design](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design) · [UI UX Pro Max](https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill) · [Emil Kowalski's skills](https://github.com/emilkowalski/skills) · [Web Interface Guidelines](https://github.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines) ## Licence MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it. The photo library (`skills/hallmark/scripts/photos.json`) lists photographs hosted on Wikimedia Commons and holds no image files. Each keeps its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and Hallmark credits every one it uses on the page. It does not use stock sites (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay), whose terms bar AI tools from picking their images.

Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents.

Studio | Quickstart | Showcase | Playground | Catalog | Docs | Discord

HyperFrames is an open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Agents and non-interactive runs should use `npx hyperframes skills update` instead — it installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 7 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs from the current `main`, so reach for it when you need the newest copy of a skill. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 7 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 7. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, publish, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/claude-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? Open-source 2D skeletal animation for games, films and interactive experiences.
Rig your art with bones and meshes, animate it, and play it anywhere with the included runtime.
Built-in MCP server: AI assistants can inspect, validate and animate your projects.


Open the editor with the Rigbytron and NILA demos, tutorials and Python scripting · Website · Documentation

▶ Watch Meet NILA: our new mascot, rigged, animated, lip-synced and rendered in Rigby2D · Also: the 75-second overview


The editor animating NILA: the head bone selected in the tree, its keys in the dopesheet, its pose in the inspector.

## Documentation **[Read the documentation](https://rigby2d.com/docs/)**: guides with screenshots for every part of the editor, the runtimes and the MCP server. The pages are also in [`docs/`](docs/). | Get started | Rig | Animate | Ship and automate | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Installation](https://rigby2d.com/docs/installation.html) | [Importing art](https://rigby2d.com/docs/importing-art.html) | [Animating](https://rigby2d.com/docs/animating.html) | [Export](https://rigby2d.com/docs/export.html) | | [Quick start](https://rigby2d.com/docs/quick-start.html) | [AutoRig](https://rigby2d.com/docs/autorig.html) | [Graph editor](https://rigby2d.com/docs/graph-editor.html) | [Runtimes](https://rigby2d.com/docs/runtimes.html) | | [The interface](https://rigby2d.com/docs/interface.html) | [Bones and slots](https://rigby2d.com/docs/bones-and-slots.html) | [Poses and faces](https://rigby2d.com/docs/poses-and-faces.html) | [Python scripting](https://rigby2d.com/docs/scripting.html) | | [Demo projects](https://rigby2d.com/docs/demos.html) | [Meshes](https://rigby2d.com/docs/meshes.html) · [Constraints](https://rigby2d.com/docs/constraints.html) | [Film](https://rigby2d.com/docs/film.html) · [Scenes](https://rigby2d.com/docs/scenes.html) · [Lip-sync](https://rigby2d.com/docs/lip-sync.html) | [AI assistants (MCP)](https://rigby2d.com/docs/mcp.html) | ## Features - **AutoRig**: a layered PSD becomes an editable rig in one step: bones, joints, bending meshes and IK. - **Full rigging toolset**: bones, weighted meshes, linked meshes, image sequences, skins, events, clipping and paths, with IK, transform, path, physics and slider constraints. - **Animation**: Setup and Animate modes, dopesheet, graph editor with Bézier handles, onion skinning, pose library, face controls and retargeting between characters. - **Film workspace**: 4K, timecode, an animatable camera, audio tracks, viseme lip-sync with on-device Whisper transcription, and renders to PNG sequences, WebM with alpha and MP4. - **Scene composition** (new in 0.3): several characters on one stage as actors with NLE-style clips (trim, speed, loops, crossfades, their own audio), painted layers with parallax, and a camera, and they play in games through every runtime. See [Scenes](https://rigby2d.com/docs/scenes.html). - **A focused editor**: Game and Film workspaces, panels you can resize or pop out to a second monitor, *Open recent*, and a searchable shortcut reference with Reference and Blender-like keys. - **Python scripting** and custom tools, and a built-in **MCP server** so AI assistants such as Claude can inspect, rig and animate your projects. - **Lossless skeleton JSON (3.8, 4.2, 4.3) and binary `.skel`** with texture atlases, played by the **JavaScript, Rust, Unity and Godot runtimes**. - Built-in **tutorials** and demo projects (**NILA**, **Rigbytron**, and a **scene** with both), also on the [Demos page](https://rigby2d.com/demos/) with their game-ready exports (demo content © Rigby2D, under its own [demo license](branding/DEMO-LICENSE.md)). ## Getting started - **In your browser:** [open the editor](https://rigby2d.com/editor/), nothing to install. - **Windows:** [download the portable editor](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/releases/latest/download/Rigby2D_x64_portable.exe) or an installer from [Releases](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/releases). - **AI assistants:** install [Rigby2D-AI.mcpb](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d/releases/latest/download/Rigby2D-AI.mcpb) in Claude Desktop, or see the [MCP guide](https://rigby2d.com/docs/mcp.html). - **From source** (Node.js 20+ and the [Tauri prerequisites](https://tauri.app/start/prerequisites/)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art/rigby2d.git cd rigby2d npm install npm run dev # desktop app; npm run web:dev for the browser, npm test for the tests ``` See [Installation](https://rigby2d.com/docs/installation.html) for every option. ## Project structure ``` src/core/ Runtime: data model, skeleton JSON/.skel + atlas I/O, pose evaluation, constraints, playback src/editor/ Editor UI: viewport, tree, inspector, dopesheet, graph editor, import/export, scripting src/webgl/ Reference WebGL renderer for the runtime src/mcp/ Model Context Protocol server for AI assistants runtimes/ Rust runtime and the Godot 4 node (preview) site/ Website and documentation site (GitHub Pages) docs/ Documentation pages and images branding/ Logo, icons, Rigbytron and NILA (proprietary, see TRADEMARKS.md) src-tauri/ Native desktop shell test/ node:test suites ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development setup, coding style and pull request process. ## License Rigby2D's source code is licensed under either of - [MIT License](LICENSE-MIT) - [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) at your option. © 2026 [jaisurya-dev-art](https://github.com/jaisurya-dev-art) Unless you state otherwise, any contribution you submit for inclusion in Rigby2D is licensed under both licenses as above, without any additional terms or conditions. See [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md). ## Disclaimer Rigby2D is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by the makers of any other animation software. All trademarks belong to their respective owners. Rigby2D reads and writes the skeleton JSON, binary `.skel` and texture atlas file formats solely for interoperability, so that users can work with their own exported files. This support was implemented clean-room: - **JSON and atlas formats:** implemented from publicly available documentation. - **Binary `.skel` format:** implemented from the publicly documented binary layout of earlier versions and by comparing JSON and binary exports of the same skeleton (black-box observation of exported data). # OpenVideoHarness **A video workbench for Claude Code and Codex. You ask for a film in one sentence; the agent writes the code that renders every frame, checks its own work, and stops at three points for your sign-off.** Science shorts, 3Blue1Brown-style explainers, launch films, music videos, data stories, paper talks, hand-drawn shorts and meme edits, with voiceover, and with music and sound effects written as code. **English** · [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Website](https://zlhad.top/OpenVideoHarness/docs/site/) · [Wiki](https://github.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/wiki) ![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-black) ![Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/agents-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex-orange) ![Engines](https://img.shields.io/badge/engines-HyperFrames%20%7C%20canvas%20%2B%20Three.js%20%7C%20p5.brush%20%7C%20Manim%20%7C%20Blender-blue) Frames from the 5 showcase films and the style library. An agent made each film from this repo's docs alone.
--- ## What it makes Each folder in [`showcase/`](showcase/) holds the request, the brief, the storyboard, the review notes and all the source: a ready starting point for a similar film. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48923404-eff1-41cd-b303-82c9ede51c1f ▶ The opening of the intro film (25 s, with sound), path-traced in Blender and driven by code. The films live in the [`media` release](https://github.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/releases/tag/media), outside git, so a clone doesn't download them. Films 00–03 were finished silent and their sound was fitted afterwards. Community films in the same vein, and how they were made, are in [`cases/`](cases/README.md); films you make with this repo are welcome in `showcase/`. ## Quick start You need macOS or Linux, Node.js 22 or later, Google Chrome, FFmpeg, Python 3 with [uv](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv), and Claude Code or Codex ([full list](#requirements-cost-and-limits)). ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/main/install.sh | bash cd ~/OpenVideoHarness && claude # or: codex ``` The installer puts the repo in `~/OpenVideoHarness` with its packages, fetches 37 read-only reference repos and registers the `open-video-harness` skill for Claude Code and Codex, so asking for a video from any folder finds it. About 650 MB on disk. Then say what you want: > Make a 30-second vertical science short: why does a low-orbit satellite's signal change pitch? English voiceover, English and Chinese subtitles. What happens next: 1. Two or three directions, each with one frame and a hook, plus an outline. You pick one. 2. A storyboard with a keyframe for every shot. 3. A first draft, with the review scores and the two or three things it likes least. The final render comes after you say yes. The wiki's [Getting Started](https://github.com/ZLHad/OpenVideoHarness/wiki/Getting-Started) walks from nothing to a first film. Say what the film is about, who it's for and where it will be shown; a long brief isn't needed. | Kind | Say | |---|---| | Math explainer | "In the 3Blue1Brown style, how a Fourier series builds a square wave, 20 seconds, readable with the sound off." | | Product film | "A 30-second launch film for my app in the ink-wash style, real screenshots only, sound effects on the key moves." | | Paper talk | "Turn the core method of `papers/main.tex` into a 3-minute explainer; copy the paper's details exactly, English narration with Chinese subtitles." | | Archive film | "A 40-second countdown film cut from public-domain NASA launch footage, with every clip's licence on record." | | Quick try | "A quick 15-second draft to see whether a cyber-glitch look suits my game trailer; don't ask me anything." | | Hands-on | "A 90-second explainer on how satellites avoid collisions, at the studio level. I'll choose the hook, the main character, the theme tune, the title and the cover; you decide the rest." | ## How it works Coding agents can already make a video from one sentence. Getting a good one every time is the hard part: the same model can be brilliant once, then lose the pacing, glow everything and invent numbers the next time, because it has no production process to follow and no way to check its work. This repo is that process and those checks, written as docs an agent follows and a CLI, `bin/vh`.

The film is code. The agent writes a page (or a Manim scene, or a Blender script) in which every frame is a function of its time t; a browser (or Manim, or Blender) draws each frame, and FFmpeg joins them with the soundtrack. An agent can't watch video or hear sound, so every step is built to be checked from frames, numbers and text. 1. **Route.** The routing table in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) picks one of the 9 video types and its workflow; your request sets the effort level and what you want to decide yourself. 2. **Gate ①: direction and outline.** Two or three concept cards, each with a frame and a hook. Picking one settles the idea, the look and the hook together, before any code is written. 3. **Gate ②: storyboard.** Every shot lists what the viewer must take in, in order and for how long, with one keyframe per shot. 4. **Sound first.** Voiceover or music comes first; every word and beat is timed, and the picture hangs on those times. 5. **Code, then check.** After each scene the agent tiles frames into a contact sheet and fixes it against a 20-point checklist, and measures the sound. A reviewer agent with a fresh context then scores the whole draft on 8 points. 6. **Gate ③: first draft.** You see the draft, its contact sheet, the scores and what the agent likes least. If you can't say what's wrong, it makes two or three versions of one passage for you to pick from. 7. **Final.** The final render goes through `bin/vh check`, and what went wrong goes into the project's `LESSONS.md`. A few rules never relax ([CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) has them all): every frame depends only on t, so any frame can be rendered alone, in parallel and in any order, and checked; when there is sound, it sets the timing; the storyboard comes before code; numbers, quotes and paper details are copied from the source, and anything uncertain stays out; API keys stay in environment variables. **How is this different from just asking an agent?** We ran one small blind comparison ([docs/research/06](docs/research/en/06-concept-first-ab.md)): two one-line requests, each made once with the workflow (at the quick level) and once with only a few floor rules, all silent. details.readme:
Website · Download · Documentation · Release notes · Roadmap · Project status · Contributing

# Horizon Horizon is Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3 rewritten in Rust: a native game that reads the same worlds, follows the same rules and generates the same terrain as the Java game, and is checked against it by 281 differential harnesses. You play it through a small launcher, on the files from your own copy of Minecraft. It is free, open source and unofficial. > Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft. Horizon contains no Minecraft code, assets or data: you need your own legally obtained copy of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3. ## Download Horizon is installed through **the Horizon launcher**. Get it from [playhorizon.dev](https://playhorizon.dev) (the Download button picks your system) or from [the launcher releases](https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon/releases?q=launcher-v&expanded=true), for Linux x86-64, macOS on Apple Silicon or Windows x64. The launcher installs and updates the game, prepares its files from your copy of Minecraft (your own install, or downloaded from Mojang for your account), and updates itself. **You need** a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft: Java Edition (the launcher signs in with it, as other launchers do; see [Microsoft account](docs/microsoft-account.md)) and a GPU with Vulkan on Linux and Windows, or any Apple Silicon Mac. Nothing else: with no Minecraft on your computer, Play downloads 26.3 and the Java it needs from Mojang for your account, as the official launcher does, then prepares it once. An install you already have (the official launcher, Prism, MultiMC and other launchers all work) is used instead. Step by step, with macOS's first-open prompt and the first launch: [Install and first launch](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/install).
## What works today The [documentation](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/) covers each of these. - **The game:** singleplayer with vanilla's world generation, mobs, villagers, raids, redstone, every command, the HUD and the recipe book, on saves in vanilla's format. Worlds from 1.8 to 26.2 are upgraded as vanilla does. [Status table](#project-status). - **Horizon's own extras:** new menus (vanilla's are one setting away), graphics presets, distant terrain up to 1024 chunks, controller support, optional zoom, minimap and more, all off by default where they would change the vanilla look. See [Settings](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/settings). - **Resource packs and data packs:** resource packs work, and data packs load functions, predicates and item modifiers. - **Playing with others:** invite friends from the pause menu's Friends button with a code, Open to LAN, and joining servers, online-mode ones with the Microsoft account the launcher signs in with. See [Multiplayer](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/multiplayer). - **Mods:** Horizon has its own mod system (Rust compiled to WebAssembly). Java mod jars do not run. See [Mods and data packs](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/mods). Screenshots, captured in the Rust client itself with vanilla assets and no mods or shaders:
## Host a server The launcher's **Servers** page creates, starts, backs up and updates a Horizon server with buttons, and invites friends over Tailscale. On a VPS, `horizon-server` installs with one command and runs without Java. Guide: [Host a server](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/hosting) ([reference](docs/hosting.md)). ## Modpacks The launcher's **Modpacks** page imports a Modrinth or CurseForge pack, shows which of its mods Horizon can carry over, and plays the ones it can as their own profile. Today that means content mods made of data and assets; mods with Java code are not ported yet. See [Modpacks](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/modpacks). ## Agent control AI agents and scripts can play Horizon. `horizon-ctl`, shipped beside the game in every release folder, is a command line that reads the game as JSON and acts like a player; `horizon-ctl mcp` serves the same commands as an MCP server (one tool per command, screenshots returned as images). ```sh horizon-ctl launch --world Survival --seed 5 --wait # finds the version the launcher installed horizon-ctl state # position, health, food, target, screen... horizon-ctl find-block birch_log # the nearest logs horizon-ctl goto -0.5 65 -2.5 --near 2.5 # walks there along a path horizon-ctl break -1 65 -3 # mines it; replies with the drops horizon-ctl open-inventory && horizon-ctl click-slot 0 # menus: slots, buttons by label, text fields ``` Commands block until the action is done and reply with what happened; errors are JSON with distinct exit codes, `horizon-ctl help` lists every command and `horizon-ctl COMMAND --help` explains one with examples. It talks to the game over a Unix socket on Linux and macOS and over a token-protected localhost port on Windows. See [Agent control in the native client guide](docs/native-client.md#agent-control-horizon-ctl-and-mcp). ## Build from source For developers. Requirements: Rust 1.90 or newer, Python 3.10 or newer, JDK 25, and on Linux the ALSA and udev development headers (`libasound2-dev libudev-dev` on Debian and Ubuntu). Development and the vanilla harnesses run on Linux. Horizon contains no game files, and `horizon-prepare` never downloads them (the launcher downloads them from Mojang only for a signed-in account that owns the game). It builds its resources from **your own copy** of Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, verified against the checksums in `research-lock.json`: 1. **Client:** install Java Edition with the official launcher and play 26.3 once. Horizon reads `versions/26.3/`, `libraries/` and `assets/` from the launcher's game directory (`~/.minecraft` on Linux). If yours lives elsewhere, pass `--minecraft-dir` or set `HORIZON_MINECRAFT_DIR`. 2. **Server jar:** the 26.3 server jar, from the `downloads.server.url` in your launcher's `versions/26.3/26.3.json` (or [minecraft.net/download/server](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server) while 26.3 is the current release). Pass it with `--server-jar` or set `HORIZON_SERVER_JAR`. It is only needed the first time. ```sh git clone https://github.com/horizon-rust/horizon.git cd horizon cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- --prepare --server-jar ~/Downloads/server.jar # needs JDK 25 cargo run --release -p horizon-prepare -- sounds # optional: sounds from your launcher install cargo run --release -p horizon-client ``` Everything prepared lands in the gitignored `.local/`. It is derived from the game: never commit it or share it. The client starts on the title screen. Command-line options (`--world`, `--seed`, `--creative`, `--render-distance`, `--dedicated`), controls, scripting through `horizon-ctl` and the architecture are described in [the native client guide](docs/native-client.md). The rest of the developer documentation is indexed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), including [the parity workflow](docs/parity-workflow.md). ## Roadmap What is being done now, what comes next and where you can help, in plain words and in technical detail: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). [playhorizon.dev/hub](https://playhorizon.dev/hub) shows it with the work board, the journal of what shipped and how to help. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how we work (vanilla first, small pull requests, labels), or [the contributing guide](https://playhorizon.dev/docs/contributing) on the site. Questions and ideas: [Discord](https://discord.gg/HcTeMZxe5E). Before opening a pull request, run the self-check and paste the block it prints: ```sh git config core.hooksPath .githooks python3 tools/pr_ready.py ``` It runs rustfmt, clippy with warnings denied, the tests of the crates you touched, the Python tests, the public-tree check, and the vanilla harnesses your change can affect. # ViFastTts — Text-to-Speech tiếng Việt [![ci](https://github.com/dvchd/ViFastTts/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dvchd/ViFastTts/actions/workflows/ci.yml) ## Cài đặt nhanh Thứ tự ưu tiên: **Windows → macOS → Linux**. Tải release portable tại [Releases](https://github.com/dvchd/ViFastTts/releases) (bản `-rc*` là pre-release, chưa ký): 1. **Windows x64:** `vifasttts-desktop-windows-x64.zip` → giải nén → chạy `vifasttts-desktop.exe` (SmartScreen: More info → Run anyway). 2. **macOS arm64:** `vifasttts-desktop-macos-arm64.zip` → kéo `ViFastTts.app` vào Applications → chuột phải **Open**. Nếu Gatekeeper chặn: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/ViFastTts.app`. 3. **Linux x64:** `vifasttts-desktop-linux-x64.tar.gz` → giải nén → `./run.sh`. 4. Desktop có sẵn **server nội bộ** + **model browser HuggingFace**; extension remote trỏ tới `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Unified binary `vifasttts` (CLI/TUI/ server) nằm cạnh app; TUI chỉ chạy từ terminal, GUI không mở TUI. 5. Android: `vifasttts-mobile-android.apk` (có tải `.vfa/.vfts` qua server); iOS: simulator-only `.zip`; extension: `extension.zip`; web: `web-dist.tar.gz`. 6. Catalog dùng chung: native `vifasttts-model-manager`; web/extension `web/shared/model-api.js`; Android/iOS gọi `/api/models/*`. Xem `docs/MODEL_SEARCH.md`. 7. Design tokens dùng chung ở `design/tokens.json`; desktop/iOS/Android/web/ extension dùng cùng palette kem–đỏ, font Be Vietnam Pro và icon thương hiệu. Hướng dẫn đầy đủ, gồm build từ source và xử lý lỗi: **`docs/INSTALL.md`**. **TTS tiếng Việt mã nguồn mở: nhỏ, nhanh, tự train được.** Toolkit nghiên cứu + triển khai TTS **một giọng**, hiểu văn bản tiếng Việt, sinh giọng 24 kHz và xuất ONNX chạy CPU. Mỗi checkpoint là một người nói, một phương ngữ — không cần `speaker_id`, `dialect_id` hay audio mẫu. [![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-C6281E)](https://www.python.org/) [![ONNX](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-ONNX%20CPU-C6281E)](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) [![Code MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-MIT-1F2430)](LICENSE) [![Model research](https://img.shields.io/badge/model-research%20%2F%20non--commercial-b45309)](docs/NGOC_HUYEN.md) [![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97-Hugging%20Face-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small) ## 0. Chạy demo Ngọc Huyền trong 2 phút ```bash git clone https://github.com/dvchd/ViFastTts.git cd ViFastTts ./scripts/run_ngochuyen_demo.sh # Windows PowerShell: # powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\run_ngochuyen_demo.ps1 # mở http://127.0.0.1:8090 ``` Script tự tải ONNX FP32 **Q-init** từ HuggingFace (có kiểm sha256), tạo `.venv-demo`, cài `onnxruntime + fastapi + uvicorn` và chạy web demo — **không cần torch**. Cần Python ≥ 3.11. - **Demo online:** https://vifasttts.hoctuthien.com/ - **Hugging Face model:** https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small - **Space demo miễn phí:** https://huggingface.co/spaces/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-demo - **Thống kê demo:** https://vifasttts.hoctuthien.com/admin - **Góp ý / báo lỗi:** form trên web và Space; admin xem tại `/admin` sau khi đặt `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (nội dung bị khoá nếu chưa đặt). - **Model/card:** `docs/NGOC_HUYEN.md` - **Model bundles:** [.vfa/.vfts](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small/tree/main/bundles) · [base N0 gốc trước Q](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-base) · [3 mẫu nghe](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small/tree/main/demo) ### Chọn đúng luồng **A. Người dùng model (không train, không cần torch):** chạy script ở trên, mở web, hoặc gọi `synthesize-onnx`; dùng checkpoint/ONNX có sẵn. Không cần MFA, không cần dữ liệu. **B. Người train model:** cài `.[dev,audio,train,onnx]`, chuẩn bị audio + transcript, chạy MFA, cache, train, eval, export. Bắt đầu ở `docs/TRAINING_N0.md` (N0) hoặc `docs/TRAINING.md` (tổng quát). > **Giấy phép model mẫu:** dataset `pnnbao-ump/ngochuyen_voice` là **CC BY-NC 4.0**. > Model Ngọc Huyền chỉ dùng **nghiên cứu/phi thương mại**; không dùng giả giọng, lừa đảo > hoặc production thương mại. Code repo là MIT. ![Luồng model N0](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small/resolve/main/assets/og-image.png) > **Đọc nhanh:** muốn hiểu kiến trúc → mục 2–3; muốn train lại → `docs/TRAINING_N0.md`; > muốn triển khai → `docs/handoff/N0_DEPLOY.md`. ## 1. Dự án làm gì? Ba khối chính, ghép lại thành một câu TTS hoàn chỉnh: ```text Văn bản ──▶ FRONTEND (tiếng Việt) ──▶ MODEL (mel + thời lượng) ──▶ VOCODER ──▶ WAV ``` | Khối | Nhiệm vụ | Điểm mạnh | | --- | --- | --- | | **Frontend** | Chuẩn hoá số/ngày/giờ/đơn vị, tách âm tiết, chuyển thành **7 ID/âm tiết** | Phủ toàn bộ tiếng Việt chuẩn, không UNK; normalizer có nhánh Bắc/Trung/Nam (mức văn bản) | | **Model acoustic** | Từ 7 ID → dự đoán mel + thời lượng + f0/vuv/energy | Non-autoregressive, chạy tất định, xuất ONNX được | | **Vocoder** | Từ mel → sóng 24 kHz | iSTFTNet nhẹ, có vòng huấn luyện GAN tham chiếu | **Khác biệt cốt lõi:** thay vì đưa chuỗi ký tự hay BPE vào model, dự án mô tả mỗi âm tiết bằng 5 thành phần ngôn ngữ học `âm đầu + âm đệm + âm chính + âm cuối + thanh điệu` (cộng dấu câu/chấm câu — xem mục 7). Nhờ vậy: phát âm ổn định, dấu thanh không bao giờ sai vị trí, và không có "từ lạ" với tiếng Việt chuẩn. ## 2. Trạng thái hiện tại (số liệu thật) | Hạng mục | Kết quả | | --- | --- | | Bộ test | **2.916 test pass / 24 skip**; `ruff` sạch | | Parser âm tiết | Vét cạn **49.104 tổ hợp = 0 lỗi**; 39K từ thật: 6.617/6.633 parse OK | | Kho âm tiết | 25 âm đầu (thêm Q) · 2 âm đệm · 15 âm chính · 11 âm cuối · 6 thanh → **264 vần** | | Model | Acoustic small **6,1M** (N0) / base **16,4M**; Vocos pretrained **13,5M** | | Sinh giọng | Web demo + `vifasttts synthesize` end-to-end (WAV 16-bit, 24 kHz); văn bản dài tự chia câu | | Runtime ONNX | `vifasttts synthesize-onnx` chạy acoustic + vocoder ONNX, iSTFT numpy (không cần PyTorch) | | Dịch vụ | FastAPI demo (`deploy/vifasttts_demo`, ONNX) · `vifasttts serve` · `synthesize-batch` · streaming | | Xuất ONNX | fp32 / fp16 / int8, batch và độ dài **động** (đã kiểm bằng onnxruntime) | | Huấn luyện | Train acoustic + train vocoder (GAN tham chiếu) + cache feature | | Dữ liệu YouTube | `vifasttts youtube-fetch`: tải audio + phụ đề kênh của bạn → clip 24 kHz mono + manifest + SRT mở + dataset card (CC BY 4.0), báo cáo từ lạ (OOV) + `--overrides` | **Model mẫu có sẵn:** **Ngọc Huyền small 6,1M** (research/non-commercial) trong GitHub release; repo không chứa file `.pt`/`.onnx` để giữ clone nhẹ — script quickstart tự tải ONNX. Muốn train giọng khác, xem `docs/TRAINING.md` + `docs/TRAINING_N0.md`. ### Model Ngọc Huyền — số đo chính | | | |---|---| | Dữ liệu | 21,57 h raw → **19,89 h sạch**; train 17,9 h | | Train | small v2_slot5, **60k bước**, ~5 h 46 trên Mac mini M6 | | Holdout | mel L1 **4,0 dB** (z 0,298); duration MAE 1,37 frame | | Free-run | **16,57 dB**; length 0,999; pause F1 **0,825** | | Thanh điệu | thật 0,9835 · copy 0,9784 · free **0,9743** | | A/B tai | **24/24** chọn model mới so P2 zero-shot | | Tốc độ thực tế | **RTF 0,045** end-to-end, ONNX CPU trên VPS (5 câu, 22,44 s audio / 1,01 s xử lý) | Chi tiết + license: **`docs/NGOC_HUYEN.md`**. > **Vocab Q:** từ commit `60b5cf9`, onset **Q** đứng cuối vocab (ID cũ không đổi) cho chữ `qu`. > Checkpoint/ONNX mới mang `vocab_version` + `vocab_hash`; artifact cũ không còn được hỗ trợ, > không dùng adapter Q→K. Bản **đang live** là Q-init (`Q = K`, bit-exact N0 Bắc cũ); > fine-tune Q 3k đã train/export nhưng **chưa chọn**; release nghe thử cũ đã xoá > (29/10/2026), artifact base/bundle nằm trên [HuggingFace](https://huggingface.co/dvchd/vifasttts-ngochuyen-small/tree/main/bundles). > Xem `docs/Q_ONSET.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/SYLLABLE_GUIDE.md`. ## 3. Luồng hoạt động trong 30 giây ```text 1) CHUẨN BỊ: WAV + CSV → manifest.jsonl (+ cache feature, kiểm coverage) 2) TRAIN: manifest → acoustic model (dự đoán mel/duration/f0) → best.pt vocoder riêng (mel → sóng) → vocoder.pt 3) SUY LUẬN: text → 7 ID/âm tiết → mel dự đoán → vocoder → out.wav 4) XUẤT: best.pt → model.onnx (chạy bằng ONNX Runtime, fp32/fp16/int8) ``` Điểm cần nhớ để hiểu code: - **Train dùng thời lượng thật** (teacher forcing); **suy luận tự dự đoán** thời lượng. - **Không sampling** — cùng đầu vào cho cùng đầu ra. - Token không phải tiếng Việt vẫn chạy được (fallback), không bao giờ crash. Chi tiết đầy đủ (tensor shape, công thức loss, số tham số): `docs/MODEL_FLOW.md`. ## 4. Cài đặt Yêu cầu Python ≥ 3.11. **Chỉ muốn tạo âm thanh ngay (ONNX, không torch):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/dvchd/ViFastTts.git cd ViFastTts ./scripts/run_ngochuyen_demo.sh # Windows: # powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\run_ngochuyen_demo.ps1 # http://127.0.0.1:8090 ``` **Phát triển / train / xuất ONNX:** ```bash python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 pip install -e ".[dev,audio,train,onnx]" ``` Bản tối thiểu (frontend/CLI, không cần torch): `pip install -e .`. ## 5. Thử nhanh ```bash # Demo web Ngọc Huyền (tải ONNX lần đầu, chạy local) ./scripts/run_ngochuyen_demo.sh # Windows PowerShell: # powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\run_ngochuyen_demo.ps1 # hoặc macOS/Linux: make demo-ngochuyen # Xem một câu được tách thành âm tiết và 5 thành phần thế nào vifasttts parse "Hôm nay trời đẹp." vifasttts parse-syllable "quốc" vifasttts check-profile "voan bình" --profile strict # cảnh báo chính tả/từ vay vifasttts g2p "quốc" --dialect south # phiên âm IPA (phân tích) # So sánh phiên âm IPA Bắc/Nam (chỉ để phân tích) python examples/g2p_demo.py # Lấy dữ liệu từ kênh YouTube của bạn (demo 1 video ngắn, cần: pip install -e ".[youtube]") vifasttts youtube-fetch "https://www.youtube.com/@codelung/videos" --out data/codelung --demo # Phiên bản CLI vifasttts --version ``` Kiểm chứng toàn bộ pipeline bằng test (tự tạo dữ liệu tí hon, train 2 bước, sinh WAV, xuất ONNX): ```bash pytest ``` ## 6. Các lệnh chính | Nhóm | Lệnh | | --- | --- | | Frontend | `vifasttts parse ""` · `parse-syllable ` · `check-profile "" --profile strict` · `g2p "" [--dialect south]` | | Dữ liệu | `build-manifest` · `validate-manifest` (kèm coverage) · `build-lexicon` · `cache-features` · `youtube-fetch` (tải kênh của bạn) | | Huấn luyện | `vifasttts train ...` · `vifasttts train-vocoder ...` | | Sinh giọng | `vifasttts synthesize --text "..." --output out.wav [--dialect south] [--speed 0.9] [--overrides file.json] [--peak-normalize]` | | Batch / dịch vụ | `synthesize-batch --input list.txt --output-dir out/` · `serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000` | | Xuất | `vifasttts export-onnx ... [--precision fp16\|int8]` · `export-vocoder-onnx ...` | | Runtime ONNX | `vifasttts synthesize-onnx --acoustic model.onnx --vocoder vocoder.onnx --text "..." --output out.wav [--provider cpu\|cuda\|coreml\|tensorrt]` | | Khác | `vifasttts --version` | | Kiểm tra | `pytest` · `ruff check .` · `mypy src/vifasttts` · `tools/parser_audit.py` · `tools/frontend_benchmark.py` · `tools/dataset_report.py` · `tools/split_manifest.py` |
Ví dụ đầy đủ (bấm để mở) ```bash # Dữ liệu: metadata.csv có dạng id|text vifasttts build-manifest --metadata data/metadata.csv --wav-dir data/wavs --output data/manifest.jsonl vifasttts validate-manifest --manifest data/manifest.jsonl --wav-dir data/wavs # Huấn luyện vifasttts train --config configs/base_24k.yaml \ --train-manifest data/train.jsonl --val-manifest data/val.jsonl --output runs/base vifasttts train-vocoder --config configs/base_24k.yaml \ --manifest data/train.jsonl --output runs/vocoder # Sinh giọng + xuất ONNX vi
